info.title: API.SH: Any website
info.description: The Any website API from API.SH: public Any website data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Monitors a page for changes: each call returns the page's text as `snapshot` (lines), a SHA-256 `hash` of it and a `snapshot_id`. Pass an earlier call's `snapshot_id` as `since` to get `changed` and a `diff` (lines added and removed, with counts), or an earlier `hash` to get `changed` only. `mode=content` (default) compares the main content (navigation, footers and ads dropped), `text` the whole visible text, `html` the markup without scripts and styles. `ignore` is a regular expression for lines to leave out (timestamps, counters). A snapshot can be compared as long as your plan keeps responses. Never served from cache.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-changes

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public http(s) URL of the page (a bare domain works too).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The `snapshot_id` (for a diff) or `hash` of an earlier call.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: What to compare.

parameters.name: ignore
parameters.description: Regular expression; matching lines are ignored.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to view the page from (default US).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The emails, phone numbers and social profiles a website publishes, read from its home page and its likely contact, about, legal-notice (impressum) and team pages (6 pages at most). `emails` are de-duplicated, including addresses written as `name [at] domain [dot] com` and protected addresses, with `own_domain` true for the site's own domain. `phones` come from click-to-call links and the site's structured data, `phones_uncertain` from numbers written in the page text; each has `e164` (international form) when the country is known (`phone_country`: the `country` parameter, else the site's country domain, language or its own click-to-call numbers). `social_profiles` covers LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest, GitHub, Telegram, WhatsApp, Threads and Snapchat (`socials` groups their URLs by platform). Every item lists in `sources` the pages it was found on; `pages_checked` lists the pages read. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-contacts

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Website URL or bare domain (e.g. example.com).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to read the site from; also the country for phone numbers written without a country code.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Reads a website breadth-first from `url`, following its own links and the URLs in its sitemap, and returns every page as clean markdown (or text / HTML). By default the crawl stays under the start URL's folder (`scope=site` for the whole site); `include` / `exclude` narrow it further. Pages the site's robots.txt disallows are not read. Each item of `pages` has url, final_url, depth, `found_in` (start, link or sitemap), HTTP status, title, description, language, author, published date, the content under the key named by `format`, word_count, `links_count` and `internal_links_count`; a page that could not be read has `error`. `totals` gives the counts (pages read and failed, URLs discovered, queued and skipped by reason) and `skipped` lists up to 100 skipped URLs with the reason (robots, filtered, not_html, out_of_scope, depth). One call reads up to 50 pages within about 75 seconds; when time runs out first, `truncated` is true and `next_urls` holds the URLs still queued (crawl them with further calls). Content is capped at 100,000 characters per page. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost. Cost: 1 credit per 2 pages of `max_pages` (default 10 = 5 credits).

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-crawl

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Start URL (a bare domain works too).

parameters.name: max_pages
parameters.description: Pages to read at most (1-50).

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.description: Link depth from the start URL (0 = the start page only; sitemap URLs count as depth 1).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Only read pages whose path matches: comma-separated globs (`*` = any characters except `/`, `**` = anything), or one regular expression between slashes.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Skip pages whose path matches (same syntax as `include`).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `path`: only pages under the start URL's folder; `site`: the whole site.

parameters.name: use_sitemap
parameters.description: Also queue the URLs listed in the site's sitemap.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format of each page's content (the content key has the same name).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to read the site from.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Live DNS records of a domain: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA and HTTPS by default (`type=all`), or any of A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA, SRV, PTR, DS, DNSKEY, RRSIG, TLSA, SVCB, HTTPS, NAPTR, SSHFP, SPF (comma-separated for several). `records` groups the answers by type with parsed fields (MX priority and exchange, SOA serial and timers, CAA tag and CA, SRV priority/weight/port/target, DS key tag and digest); `answers` lists them all with TTLs; `status` is NOERROR, NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL; `dnssec_validated` tells whether the answers were DNSSEC-validated. With `type=all` it also returns `email` (MX hosts, SPF record, DMARC record and policy) and the domain-verification TXT records it found. Pass an IP address for its reverse (PTR) name. Use `_dmarc.example.com`, `_sip._tcp.example.com` and similar names directly.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-dns

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, service name (_dmarc.example.com) or IP address (reverse lookup).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Record type, several comma-separated, or all.

parameters.name: dnssec
parameters.description: Ask for DNSSEC records (RRSIG) with the answers.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Structured data from any web page
get.description:
Turns any public web page into structured JSON (`redirected` is true when the url led to a different page, e.g. a retired product sent to the home page or its category: the data then describes that page). With `type=auto` the page type is detected (product, product list, article, job posting, real-estate or vehicle listing, review list, event, organization, recipe; `webpage` when none applies) and `data` holds normalized fields for that type: for a product name, brand, sku/gtin/mpn, price, currency, availability, original_price, rating, review_count, images, description, seller, variants, breadcrumbs and specs; for an article headline, authors, published_at, modified_at, publisher, image and body_text; for a job title, company, location, remote, salary range and period, employment_type, posted_at, valid_through, description and apply_url; for a listing title, price, address, location and attributes; for an event start/end, venue, address and offers; for an organization name, url, logo, same_as, address and the phone/email it publishes in its structured data. `sources` lists the page signals used (json-ld, microdata, rdfa, opengraph, app_state, shopify, woocommerce, greenhouse, page_text) and `raw` carries every JSON-LD block, the OpenGraph/Twitter meta and the page's embedded app data. Pages that need a login are not supported. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-extract

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public http(s) URL of the page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Page type to extract; `auto` detects it.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to view the page from (prices, language and availability can differ by country).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: RSS / Atom feed reader and discovery
get.description:
Reads an RSS (0.9x, 1.0, 2.0), Atom or JSON Feed. Give the feed URL, or any page or site: the feeds it links to are found (and common feed paths tried) and the first one is read; `discovered` lists every feed found. Returns the feed's title, description, link, language, image, last update and generator, and its items with id, title, link, published and updated dates, author, a plain-text summary (up to 1,000 characters; full article texts are not returned), categories, image, comments link and enclosures (podcast audio, media).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-feed

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Feed URL, or a page or site to find the feed on.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items at most (default 50, max 500).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to view the page from (default US).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: All images on a web page
get.description: Every image on a page: `` tags (including lazy-load attributes such as data-src and data-srcset), `` sources, inline CSS backgrounds, linked image files, Open Graph images and icons. Each has the absolute URL, where it was found (`source`), alt text, title, declared width and height, loading mode, format and the srcset candidates. Filter by `min_width`; pages with `page` / `next_page` (null on the last page). Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost. Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-images

get.summary: All links on a page (with broken-link check)
get.description:
Every link on a page: absolute URL, anchor text (or image alt / aria-label), internal or external, scheme (https, mailto, tel ...), rel, nofollow (nofollow, ugc or sponsored), target and how often it occurs. `type` keeps internal or external links only. `check=true` also requests each http(s) link (up to `check_limit`) and adds its HTTP status, final URL after redirects, response time and `broken` (4xx/5xx; null when the site rate-limited or could not be reached); `checked` and `broken` count them.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-links

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-logo

get.description:
The text of a public PDF file, page by page, with its metadata: title, author, subject, keywords, creator and producer, creation and modification dates, PDF version, page count and size. `text` joins the pages; `pages` has each page's text. Read up to 50 pages by default (`max_pages` up to 200) or pick pages with `pages=1-5,8`; `next_pages` names the next range when more remain. Files up to 4 MB. Scanned PDFs without a text layer come back with empty page text and `has_text: false`; password-protected files answer 400.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 4 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-pdf

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: Pages to read, e.g. `1-5`, `3`, `1-3,10,20-` (default the first `max_pages`).

parameters.name: max_pages
parameters.description: Most pages to read (default 50, up to 200).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to download the file from (default US).

get.summary: Web search with page content for AI
get.description:
Searches the web for `q` and returns the top result pages read in full as clean markdown (or text / HTML), ready for an AI model or a RAG pipeline. Each item of `results` has the search position, title, url and description from the results page, then `status` (`ok` or `failed`), the page's own title, description, language, author and published date, the content under the key named by `format` (`markdown`, `text` or `html`), `word_count` and `truncated` (content is capped at 100,000 characters per page). A page that could not be read is listed with `status: failed` and `error`; the call succeeds when at least one page was read (`pages_fetched`, `pages_failed`). `more_results` lists the other search hits without content. When `q` is itself a URL, that page alone is read. `engine` says which search engine answered (`auto` uses Google first, then Bing, then DuckDuckGo). `include_domains` and `exclude_domains` limit the results to or away from some sites. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost. Cost: 9 credits for the search plus 1 per page read (`max_results`; default 3 = 12 credits).

Price: 8 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query, or a URL to read directly.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: Result pages to read (1-10).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country to search and read the pages from.

get.description:
An on-page SEO audit of any URL: a 0-100 `score` and `issues` (error / warning / notice with a code and message: missing or long title and description, missing or multiple H1, canonical problems, noindex, robots.txt blocking, missing viewport or lang, images without alt, not HTTPS, redirect chains, thin content, missing Open Graph or structured data, robots.txt without sitemap, links without text). Also the title and description with lengths, keywords, canonical(s), robots meta and X-Robots-Tag with `indexable` / `follow`, language, charset, viewport, hreflang alternates, AMP URL, rel prev/next, heading counts and the headings outline, word count, image stats (missing alt, empty alt, missing dimensions), link stats (internal, external, nofollow, without text), structured-data types, Open Graph and Twitter tags, favicon, robots.txt (found, sitemaps, whether it allows this page), HTTP status, redirect chain, response time, HTML size, server, compression and cache headers.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-seo

get.description:
Every URL a site lists in its XML sitemaps: the sitemaps are found from robots.txt (or /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml), sitemap indexes are followed, gzip sitemaps and plain-text sitemaps are read. The first page also lists `sitemaps` (with lastmod for sitemaps named in an index). Each URL has lastmod, changefreq, priority, image and video counts, hreflang alternates (`alternates=true`; their count otherwise), the news title for news sitemaps and the sitemap it came from. Pass `sitemap` to read one sitemap only. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page. Each call answers within about 45 s: for slow sites a page can hold fewer than `limit` URLs (`time_limited: true`); continue with `next_cursor`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-sitemap

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Site (home page or domain), or a sitemap URL.

parameters.name: sitemap
parameters.description: Read only this sitemap (or sitemap index).

parameters.name: alternates
parameters.description: List each URL's hreflang alternates (language, URL); without it `alternates` is their count.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: URLs per page (default 1000, max 10000).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pass `next_cursor` from the previous response; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Subdomains of a domain found in public certificate-transparency logs (every publicly trusted TLS certificate is logged): each name with whether it is a wildcard, when it was first and last seen in a certificate, when its newest certificate expires, how many certificates name it and their issuers. `total` counts all names found; `certificates` the certificates read. Only names with a currently valid certificate by default; `include_expired=true` adds names whose certificates have all expired (older infrastructure). Domains with very many certificates can take up to a minute. When the main log search is down, the answer comes from current certificates only and says so with `current_certificates_only: true` (and `complete: false` if it stopped early). Pages with `page` / `next_page` (null on the last page).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-subdomains

parameters.description: Include wildcard names (*.example.com). Default true.

parameters.description: Names per page (default 1000, max 5000).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The technologies a website runs, detected from its response headers, cookies, meta tags, HTML, script URLs, inline scripts, styles and page elements with an open fingerprint set of thousands of technologies: CMS, e-commerce platform, JavaScript frameworks and libraries, UI frameworks, analytics, tag managers, advertising, marketing automation, live chat, payment processors, CDN, hosting/PaaS, web servers, programming language, databases, security, cookie-consent tools and more. Each item has name, version (where the page shows it), confidence (0-100), categories, website, description, icon, CPE and what it was detected by (implied technologies, such as PHP under WordPress, say `implied`). Also `by_category`, the `server` and `x-powered-by` headers.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-technologies

get.description:
Registration data of a domain from its registry, the way WHOIS shows it: registered, updated and expiry dates, age and days until expiry, status codes, registrar (name, IANA id, website, abuse email and phone), name servers, DNSSEC (signed, DS records), the registry's WHOIS server and every event. For gTLDs and most ccTLDs the registry's structured data is used, merged with the registrar's own record; for registries without it (.io, .de, .jp, .co and others) their WHOIS server is read and parsed. A subdomain is resolved to its registered name (www.example.co.uk -> example.co.uk). Unregistered names answer `registered: false`. Contacts keep only organization, state and country (names, emails, phones and addresses of people are never returned). `raw=true` adds the registry's record (or the WHOIS text without personal contact lines).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/web-whois

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name (a URL or subdomain works too).

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Also return the registry's full record (`raw`) or WHOIS text (`raw_text`).

parameters.name: registrar_lookup
parameters.description: Also read the registrar's own record (thin registries such as .com/.net). Default true.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.
